hook: Content note: SCP-3929 sits behind an adult-content warning and is packed with crude sexual language and explicit descriptions of what test subjects do. It is a comedy about a bottle of brown knock-off pills from an anomalous drug-maker and Person of Interest called dado, and most of the jokes come from the Foundation reporting absurd results with a straight face. If crude humour is not for you, this one is easy to skip.
whyItMatters: The whole article runs on literal-mindedness: a scammer asks for a cheap Viagra substitute that makes old people horny, and dado delivers exactly that, a pill that makes the taker old and horny. The humour comes from pairing clinical symptom lists and test logs with increasingly unhinged emails and quotes. It is a reminder that the format can carry farce as easily as horror.
thingsToNotice:
Over about four hours the drug ages the user by seventy years or more while pushing their libido far past anything normal, and it still does nothing for sexual dysfunction. The email thread escalates from a buyer demanding cheap fakes for a scam to that same buyer, mid-dose, complaining about wrinkling skin and testicles hanging to his knees before propositioning dado. The test log keeps the deadpan going: one man grinds against a chair, a woman is restrained three times for trying to force her fist into her vagina and keeps urging staff to push a whole leg in, a footnoted subject aged past two hundred wants a doctor's head forced inside her, and a woman who took two capsules turns into ash within five minutes, ash that leaves the attendants feeling sexually uncomfortable.

The twist is Trial #14. An asexual subject ages backwards to about two weeks old while talking more and more passionately about kites, and Dr. McElroy's footnote explains that for asexual subjects the drug amplifies niche hobbies instead. His aside about a long conversation with a toddler on Frasier Crane's psychological development is the closing punchline.
